value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Highland.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Two sets of plans and two sets of structural calculations (in-person)
Notarized authorization letter (if a representative signs)

value: Schedule inspection through the city's inspection line
Approved plans and job card must remain on-site during construction

value.notes: Electronic portal submittals are typically reviewed within 1-3 business days (most same-day); standard in-person review is expedited to 1-2 days. SolarAPP+ provides instant approval eligibility determination.

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ (fastest option) / standard permitting (all other systems)
other_conditions: SolarAPP+ pathway limited to rooftop installations on primary dwellings, licensed contractors only, up to 38.4kW AC, excludes ground-mounted or ballasted systems
Any ground-mounted system or roof-mounted system on a Historic-designated structure requires Planning Division approval before a building permit can be issued

permit_fees.notes: The page states application fees are collected at submittal, and that SolarAPP+ includes a processing fee covering up to three revisions, but does not state specific dollar amounts.
